context.analysis:
## Overview
[A real-time payment fraud screening system for a mid-size payment processor that evaluates card-not-present authorizations against fraud models before approval. It provides case management for fraud analysts while ensuring strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and sub-50ms latency.]

## Key Elements
* Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems (External Software System)
* Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening (Core Software System)
* Fraud Analyst, Merchant Risk Manager, and Compliance / Auditor Officer (Internal Persons)
* Card Networks / Tokenization Vaults (External Software System)
* Core Banking / Ledger Systems (External Software System)

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway -> Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening: REST/JSON over HTTPS with mTLS and OAuth2/JWT validation (Synchronous Ingress)
* Fraud Analyst -> Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening: HTTPS via Web UI for case management
* Merchant Risk Manager -> Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening: HTTPS via Web Dashboard for KPIs and rule efficacy
* Compliance Officer -> Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening: Secure Read-Only API/Console for audit trails
* Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening -> Core Banking / Ledger Systems: Asynchronous message queues using AWS SQS/SNS

## Technology Stack
* Cloud Platform: AWS (eu-west-1 region) utilizing managed services (RDS, SQS, ElastiCache) to minimize operational overhead for a 3-engineer team
* Compute: AWS Graviton-based instances with auto-scaling provisioned concurrency to stay within the €25,000/month budget at 3,000 TPS
* Security & Auditing: AWS KMS with annual key rotation and AWS S3 Object Lock in compliance mode for tamper-evident 7-year audit storage
* Observability: AWS X-Ray for distributed tracing to isolate latency bottlenecks within the 50ms P99 window

## Rationale
[This architecture balances extreme performance requirements (3,000 TPS under 50ms P99 latency) with strict regulatory mandates (PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year tamper-evident auditing). By leveraging fully managed AWS services, an externalized tokenization/enrichment pattern, and a small engineering team, it achieves high availability and security within a strict €25,000 monthly budget.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform hosted on AWS in `eu-west-1` that evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations and manages analyst reviews. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and sub-50ms P99 decision latency while operating within a strict 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Fraud Analyst, Merchant Risk Manager, Compliance / Auditor Officer
- **External Systems**: Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems, Card Networks / Tokenization Vaults, Core Banking / Ledger Systems
- **Containers**: AWS API Gateway, Real-Time Scoring Engine (ECS Fargate), Case Management Backend (ECS Fargate)
- **Data Stores & Brokers**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon S3, Amazon ElastiCache (Redis), Amazon SQS

## Relationships
- **Payment Gateway** --(HTTPS/REST)--> **AWS API Gateway**
- **AWS API Gateway** --(HTTP/gRPC with mTLS)--> **Real-Time Scoring Engine**
- **Real-Time Scoring Engine** --(Redis Protocol)--> **Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)**
- **Real-Time Scoring Engine & Case Management** --(AWS SDK/SQS API)--> **Amazon SQS**
- **Case Management Backend** --(HTTPS with mTLS)--> **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL**

## Technology Stack
- **AWS ECS Fargate**: Container orchestration for low-overhead, zero-downtime blue/green deployments.
- **Go / Java**: High-performance languages for the Real-Time Scoring Engine to meet the <50ms P99 latency SLA.
- **Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)**: In-memory feature store for rapid fraud rule evaluation.
- **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL & Amazon S3**: Secure relational storage with cryptographic HMAC-SHA256 audit chaining and WORM storage.
- **AWS SQS**: Lightweight, managed asynchronous event messaging to fit within the 3-engineer operational capacity.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services (ECS Fargate, SQS, ElastiCache) to meet strict sub-50ms latency and high-availability demands while minimizing operational overhead for a three-engineer team. Security controls, encryption, and tamper-evident audit logs ensure PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance within budget.

AWS API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
[The AWS API Gateway component ingests and securely routes real-time payment authorization traffic for fraud screening while enforcing strict perimeter security and compliance. It acts as the high-performance entry point for incoming card-not-present payment requests before they reach scoring engines.]

## Key Elements
- HTTP API Route Resolver (Amazon API Gateway): Terminates TLS 1.3 and enforces native JSON schema validation.
- Edge Rate Limiter & WAF (AWS WAF): Mitigates DDoS attacks and enforces rate limits.
- Upstream Integration: Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems sending authorization requests.
- Downstream Integration: Real-Time Scoring Engine hosted on AWS ECS Fargate.

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems -> HTTP API Route Resolver: Sends payment authorization requests [HTTPS/REST]
- HTTP API Route Resolver -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Routes validated authorization traffic [gRPC with mTLS via VPC Private Link]
- HTTP API Route Resolver -> AWS WAF: Inspects incoming payloads for malicious traffic [Internal AWS Integration]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon API Gateway (HTTP APIs): Selected for lower latency, zero compute overhead, and cost efficiency.
- AWS WAF: Provides managed core rule sets and custom rate-based rules for volumetric protection.
- Terraform / AWS CDK: Used for GitOps-based infrastructure deployment and configuration management.
- AWS Secrets Manager: Manages automated rotation of mTLS client certificates and secrets.

## Rationale
[This serverless edge architecture eliminates cold-start overhead to consistently meet the P99 latency target below 50 ms at 3,000 TPS. Furthermore, it strictly enforces PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and data minimization while operating efficiently within the fixed monthly budget.]

Real-Time Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to prevent fraud while enabling compliance-driven review workflows. It delivers high-performance risk decisions with strict P99 latency controls and tamper-evident auditability.

## Key Elements
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go, AWS EC2)
- Rule Evaluation Component (Go)
- Feature Aggregator Component (Go)
- Model & Rule Registry Component (Go)
- Explainability Engine Component (Go)
- Audit Trail Emitter (Go)
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)
- Amazon SQS
- Amazon S3

## Relationships
- AWS API Gateway -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Routes authorization traffic [HTTP/gRPC with mTLS]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Retrieves velocity counters and features [Redis Protocol with TLS/AUTH]
- Model & Rule Registry Component -> Amazon S3: Downloads immutable rules and model weights [HTTPS]
- Audit Trail Emitter -> Amazon SQS: Pushes cryptographically signed decision payloads [AWS SDK/SQS API]

## Technology Stack
- Go: Selected for zero-garbage-collection pauses to meet the sub-50ms latency requirement.
- AWS EC2: Replaced Fargate to eliminate cold starts and guarantee predictable CPU performance.
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Provides high-speed in-memory feature storage for low-latency rule evaluation.
- AWS KMS: Used by the Audit Trail Emitter to cryptographically sign decision payloads for tamper-evidence.
- Amazon S3: Stores versioned machine learning models and fraud rules for zero-downtime hot-reloading.

## Rationale
This architecture uses Go binaries on provisioned AWS EC2 instances to consistently achieve sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS. Furthermore, it incorporates asynchronous audit logging, cryptographic model verification, and automated fail-open circuits to satisfy strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and budget constraints.

Case Management Backend.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management Backend is an AWS ECS Fargate-based container service that processes asynchronous flagged payment events and provides a secure portal for fraud analysts to review suspicious transactions. It ensures strict 7-year auditability and PCI-DSS compliance while supporting real-time decision workflows for a 3-engineer team.

## Key Elements
- **API Controller Component**: RESTful interface handling authentication, RBAC, input validation, and bulk case operations over HTTPS.
- **Case Workflow Engine Component**: Manages case states (Open, Under Review, Resolved) and bulk resolution logic.
- **Event Consumer Component**: Subscribes to Amazon SQS to ingest flagged transaction payloads and hydrate case records.
- **Audit Logger Component**: Streams immutable records to S3 Object Lock (Compliance Mode) and maintains an indexed metadata view in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.
- **SLA Metrics Component**: Calculates time-to-decision metrics for compliance and operational tracking.
- **RDS Proxy**: Manages database connection pooling between ECS Fargate tasks and Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst / Merchant Risk Manager -> API Controller Component: Reviews cases and monitors metrics via [HTTPS] with [mTLS] and [OAuth2/OIDC]
- Event Consumer Component -> Amazon SQS: Consumes transaction messages via [AWS SDK / SQS API]
- Case Workflow Engine Component -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Persists case records and SLA metrics via [RDS Proxy] using [mTLS] and [AWS IAM]
- Audit Logger Component -> Amazon S3: Stores tamper-evident logs via [AWS SDK / S3 API] with [Object Lock]

## Technology Stack
- **Compute**: AWS ECS Fargate to minimize operational overhead for a 3-engineer team within the €25k/month budget.
- **Language**: TypeScript/Node.js or Go for rapid development and high concurrency.
- **Database**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL backed by RDS Proxy to handle connection pooling and failovers.
- **Storage**: Amazon S3 with Object Lock (Compliance Mode) for 7-year tamper-evident audit logging (R-06).
- **Messaging**: Amazon SQS with a Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) for asynchronous event ingestion.
- **Security**: AWS Secrets Manager, AWS KMS, AWS X-Ray, and OAuth2/OIDC with MFA.

## Rationale
This architecture balances strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability with a lean operational model suited for a 3-engineer team. Leveraging managed AWS services like ECS Fargate, S3 Object Lock, and RDS Proxy ensures high availability and resilience within the €25,000 monthly budget.

Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present authorizations and provides case management for fraud analysts. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while maintaining sub-50ms latency and 7-year auditability.

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analyst, Merchant Risk Manager, Compliance / Auditor Officer
* AWS API Gateway
* Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go / Java, AWS ECS Fargate)
* Case Management Backend (AWS ECS Fargate)
* Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL)
* Amazon S3 (Amazon S3)
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) (Amazon ElastiCache (Redis))
* Amazon SQS (AWS SQS)
* Amazon RDS Proxy

## Relationships
* Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Amazon SQS: Pushes decision audit payloads [HTTPS / AWS SDK]
* Case Management Backend -> Amazon RDS Proxy: Reads and writes case data and transaction records [PostgreSQL wire protocol over TLS 1.3]
* Amazon RDS Proxy -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Manages connection pooling and routes queries [PostgreSQL wire protocol over TLS 1.3]
* Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Queries real-time feature stores [RESP over TCP with TLS]

## Technology Stack
* AWS ECS Fargate: Provides serverless container orchestration within a 3-engineer team limit.
* Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Relational storage for active case management and transaction history.
* Amazon RDS Proxy: Handles connection pooling and prevents thread exhaustion under high load.
* Amazon S3 with WORM storage: Provides immutable, tamper-evident 7-year audit log retention.
* AWS KMS & Secrets Manager: Enforces encryption-at-rest and eliminates static credentials.

## Rationale
This architecture decouples high-volume audit logging via Amazon SQS and utilizes RDS Proxy to protect Aurora PostgreSQL, ensuring P99 latency remains below 50 ms. It strictly enforces PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability while operating within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

Amazon S3.analysis:
## Overview
This architecture details the Amazon S3 storage container for a real-time payment fraud screening system on AWS. It provides secure, WORM-compliant, 7-year audit retention and pseudonymized analytics within PCI-DSS Level 1 constraints.

## Key Elements
- **Bucket Policy Enforcer (IAM / AWS Lake Formation)**: Manages fine-grained access control and IAM conditions.
- **Object Lock & Vault Manager (S3 Object Lock)**: Enforces Write-Once-Read-Many (WORM) compliance in Compliance Mode.
- **Server-Side Encryption Engine (AWS KMS)**: Applies envelope encryption using customer-managed keys (CMK).
- **S3 Lifecycle Engine (AWS S3 Lifecycle)**: Manages automated tiering from Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
- **Athena Query Gateway (Amazon Athena)**: Executes sanitized queries over partitioned audit data.
- **Merchant Risk Manager & Compliance Officer**: External personas querying reporting and audit logs.

## Relationships
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Object Lock & Vault Manager: Writes decision audit payloads via AWS SDK (HTTPS/TLS 1.3).
- Compliance Officer -> Bucket Policy Enforcer: Queries archived audit logs via AWS Management Console / Athena (HTTPS).
- Merchant Risk Manager -> Athena Query Gateway: Queries pseudonymized fraud trends via BI tools (HTTPS).
- Athena Query Gateway -> Object Lock & Vault Manager: Reads parquet-formatted audit partitions via internal AWS backbone.
- DevOps Specialist -> S3 Lifecycle Engine: Manages automated tiering policies via Terraform (IaC).

## Technology Stack
- **Amazon S3**: Core object storage providing 99.999999999% durability and S3 Object Lock for tamper-evident retention.
- **AWS KMS**: AES-256 envelope encryption with annual key rotation to satisfy PCI-DSS data protection requirements.
- **Amazon Athena**: Serverless query service enabling analytics on stored audit data without managing infrastructure.
- **AWS Glue / Lambda**: Compacts raw JSON logs into compressed Apache Parquet format to optimize query costs.
- **Terraform (HashiCorp)**: Infrastructure as Code for automated, drift-free deployment by a three-engineer team.

## Rationale
This architecture meets the 7-year tamper-evident audit and PCI-DSS Level 1 requirements through S3 Object Lock and KMS encryption. Automated lifecycle tiering and Parquet compaction optimize storage and query costs to respect the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

Amazon ElastiCache (Redis).analysis:
## Overview
The system provides real-time payment fraud screening for card-not-present transactions, evaluating authorizations and managing review cases for fraud analysts. It utilizes Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) as an in-memory feature store to deliver low-latency velocity metrics for fraud rule evaluation.

## Key Elements
- Feature Store Engine (Redis OSS): In-memory key-value store holding pre-computed user/device velocity metrics.
- Replication Manager: Handles asynchronous replication across Multi-AZ nodes for high availability.
- Write-Through Ingestion Handler: Manages asynchronous updates to feature states without blocking scoring.
- Real-Time Scoring Engine: Reads velocity features via RESP protocol over TCP.
- Ingestion Pipeline / SQS: Sends asynchronous update events to refresh feature metrics.

## Relationships
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Feature Store Engine (Redis OSS): Retrieves features [RESP Protocol over TCP with TLS]
- Ingestion Pipeline / SQS -> Write-Through Ingestion Handler: Updates feature metrics [RESP Protocol over TCP with TLS]
- Feature Store Engine (Redis OSS) -> Amazon S3 / Aurora PostgreSQL: Performs periodic persistence for disaster recovery

## Technology Stack
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): In-memory data store using `cache.m6g` instances for sub-50ms P99 latency within budget.
- Redis Cluster & Multi-AZ: Ensures high availability and automatic failover under 3,000 req/sec traffic.
- Redis AUTH / RBAC & Command Whitelisting: Restricts access and disables administrative commands like `FLUSHALL` for PCI-DSS compliance.
- AWS CloudWatch: Monitors `EngineCPUUtilization`, slow logs, and memory metrics for operational visibility.

## Rationale
This architecture decouples the high-throughput read path from the ingestion write path, guaranteeing P99 decision latencies below 50 ms. Using a fully managed AWS ElastiCache service minimizes operational overhead for a three-engineer team while satisfying strict PCI-DSS Level 1 security and budget constraints.

Amazon SQS.analysis:
## Overview
This system provides real-time payment fraud screening for card-not-present transactions, evaluating authorizations and routing suspicious cases to analysts. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while maintaining sub-50ms latency at 3,000 TPS within a fixed monthly budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst, Merchant Risk Manager, Compliance / Auditor Officer
- AWS API Gateway
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go / Java, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Backend (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
- Amazon S3
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)
- Amazon SQS (Standard Queue, Dead-Letter Queue)

## Relationships
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Amazon SQS: Sends asynchronous telemetry/audit events [AWS SDK/SQS API via Interface VPC Endpoint]
- Case Management Backend -> Amazon SQS: Consumes messages via Long Polling and DeleteMessage [AWS SDK/SQS API via Interface VPC Endpoint]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL / Amazon ElastiCache: Reads rules/models and writes audit logs [SQL / Redis Protocol]
- Fraud Analyst -> AWS API Gateway: Reviews flagged cases [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration chosen for low operational overhead and scalability for a 3-person team.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Relational storage providing ACID compliance for secure 7-year audit retention.
- Amazon SQS: Managed message broker utilizing batching and VPC endpoints for decoupled, high-throughput asynchronous processing.
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): In-memory caching layer ensuring low-latency rule lookups to meet the <50ms P99 latency constraint.

## Rationale
The architecture combines managed serverless and containerized AWS services to handle 3,000 TPS under a strict €25,000 monthly budget. Asynchronous decoupling via SQS protects payment availability and checkout performance while satisfying rigorous PCI-DSS and auditability mandates.
